            # https://github.com/pytoolz/toolz/issues/387

        else:
            # ``len(seq)`` is trusted to slice the final, shorter partition.
            # Sanity-check it against the actual contents: a buggy
            # ``__len__`` would otherwise silently corrupt the output.
            if not (cut and prev[cut - 1] is not no_pad
                    and prev[cut] is no_pad):
                raise LookupError(
                    "partition_all: %r reports a __len__ inconsistent with "
                    "its contents" % (seq,))
        yield prev[:cut]
    else:

part.text:
The fix is complete and verified.

## Summary

The bug was in `partition_all` at `toolz/itertoolz.py:731`. The final, partial partition is sliced using `len(seq) % n` as a fast path when `__len__` is available, but that value was trusted blindly. A misreported `__len__` produced a silently-wrong slice.

The fix computes `cut = len(seq) % n` and, in the `__len__` fast path, validates that `cut` actually sits at the boundary between real elements and `no_pad` padding in the final tuple (`prev[cut-1]` is real, `prev[cut]` is the sentinel). If not, it raises `LookupError`. The no-`__len__` binary-search path (which finds the true cut from the data) is unchanged, and the full-partition path never consulted `len(seq)` and remains untouched — so correct sequences behave exactly as before.
